name: Lazarus Group
description: Lazarus Group is North Korea's flagship state-sponsored hacking apparatus, run by the Reconnaissance General Bureau, spanning espionage, destructive attacks, and the regime's primary hard-currency revenue stream via cryptocurrency theft. Through the first four months of 2026, TRM Labs attributes roughly $577M in stolen crypto to the group â€” about 76% of all global crypto theft this year. Its Contagious Interview / DeceptiveDevelopment fake-recruiter operation continues to trojanize developers via staged coding interviews, delivering BeaverTail and InvisibleFerret through malicious Git repos and npm/PyPI packages. In early 2026 the group was also tied to a supply-chain compromise of the widely used axios npm package and to deploying Medusa ransomware against US healthcare and Middle East targets, broadening its activity beyond pure crypto theft.

ttps.notes: Fake recruiter outreach on LinkedIn, Telegram, and Discord drives victims to staged interview/coding-test sites

ttps.technique_name: Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain
ttps.notes: Malicious npm/PyPI packages (e.g. compromised axios releases, 'graphalgo'/'bigmathutils' campaign) and trojanized GitHub repos
BeaverTail JS-based infostealer delivered via Git post-install/post-merge hooks

ttps.technique_name: Event Triggered Execution: Unix Shell Configuration Modification
ttps.notes: Malicious payloads planted in .git/hooks (post-merge, pre-push) as second-stage loaders
Heavy use of fileless/RAM-resident malware and obfuscated JS/Python loaders to evade EDR
Victims run trojanized coding-challenge repos or fake video-conferencing apps during sham interviews
Lazarus subcluster (Andariel/Stonefly-linked) deploying Medusa ransomware against healthcare targets
InvisibleFerret Python backdoor establishes persistent remote access tunnels post-infection

notable_techniques: Contagious Interview / DeceptiveDevelopment â€” fake recruiters lure developers through full sham interview pipelines, hiding loaders inside .git/hooks of coding-test repos
Operation Marstech Mayhem â€” 'Marstech1' implant scans for Exodus, Atomic, and MetaMask wallet files across Windows, macOS, and Linux and exfiltrates private keys
Brandjacked and hijacked maintainer accounts used to push malicious versions of high-traffic npm packages (e.g. axios, with 100M+ weekly downloads)
Single npm packages (e.g. 'bigmathutils') published clean first, then updated with malicious payloads after building download trust (10,000+ downloads)
Pivot into Medusa ransomware operations against US healthcare and Middle East targets, blending espionage tooling with for-profit extortion
Crypto theft proceeds laundered through mixers and cross-chain bridges to fund DPRK weapons programs
detection_opportunities: New or modified scripts in .git/hooks/ (post-merge, post-checkout, pre-push) within cloned repositories
Outbound connections from developer workstations to npm/PyPI-hosted C2 infrastructure shortly after package install
postinstall/preinstall scripts in package.json fetching remote payloads from non-registry domains
Recruiter contact via LinkedIn/Telegram/Discord followed by requests to clone and run external code as part of an 'interview'
Process memory scanning for fileless RAT activity (no payload written to disk) on developer and crypto-custody endpoints
Unexpected wallet directory access (Exodus, Atomic, MetaMask, Electrum) by unrelated processes
Sudden encryption activity on healthcare endpoints preceded by Lazarus-associated initial-access tooling (Medusa ransomware)
response_playbook: Scan developer workstations and recently cloned repos for malicious .git/hooks scripts (post-merge, post-checkout, pre-push).
Audit recently installed npm/PyPI packages for postinstall/preinstall scripts contacting non-registry domains.
Check crypto wallet directories (Exodus, Atomic, MetaMask, Electrum) for access by unrelated processes.
If a 'job interview' or recruiter contact requested cloning/running external code, treat the developer's workstation as compromised and isolate it.
Monitor for fileless RAT memory indicators (BeaverTail/InvisibleFerret) on developer endpoints.
Watch for ransomware-style encryption activity (Medusa) on healthcare-adjacent systems following any Lazarus-linked initial access.
